To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RGS domain fragment and ΔDIX mutant of rAxin induce axis formation, the ΔDIX rAxin mutant has a weaker ventralizing activity than wild‐type rAxi, and the rAxin mutant containing the RGS and βGSK3 binding domains affects both the dorsal and the ventral sides of the embryos.
the RGS domain of rat Axin is important for inhibition of Wnt signal in early Xenopus development.
the RGS and DIX domains are important for the ventralizing activities and the C‐termini of rAxin are important for the dorsalizing activity of the molecule
In summary, our research is concerned with
the roles of rAxin domains in axis formation in Xenpus embryos.
the effects of rAxin mutants on axis formation.
the role of the Axin RGS domain and APC‐binding domain in axis formation in Xenopsis embryos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RGS domain of rAxin is necessary and sufficient to induce axis formation, but the DIX domain and C‐terminus contribute to the inhibition of axis formation in Xenapus embryos.
the RGS domain of rAxin is sufficient to induce axis formation, and the C‐termini of rAxin are involved in the inhibition of WNT signaling.
the RGS domain, but not the DIX domain, is important for the ventralizing activities and axis formation in Xenopsis embryos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RGS domain of Axin is important for inhibition of Wnt‐dependent axis formation, and the DIX domain is also involved in inhibition of axis induction, but is dispensable for the inhibition of WNT‐dependent axis formation.
the RGS domain of rAxin plays a major role in the regulation of axis formation in Xenopsis laevis embryos.
the RGS and the C‐termini of rAxin are involved in axis formation, whereas the RGS domain and GSK3‐binding domain are involved in ventralization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Axin has a role in the early Xenopus embryo that is distinct from its role in Wnt‐mediated axis formation in Xenous embryos.

the RGS domain and the DIX domain are important for inhibition of the Wnt pathway in Xenopus embryos, and the GSK3β and APC‐binding domains are important for the regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway.
the C‐terminal region of Axin is required for the full inhibition of axis formation in Xenopuse embryos.
